musicalForm.repeatConfidence: All pinned canonical marks inspected: section_bar, bar and vibhag only; no repeat or alternative-ending marks. Final line has two section_bar marks at cell 12. Printed pages show the complete traversal and terminal bars. No extra verse/refrain/stanza repeats inferred.
musicalForm.sectionCaveat: All 16 canonical lines are labelled sthayi. Provenance describes its checked first six lines as sthayi through first antara, but provides no separate section boundaries. Keep encoded labels without imposing an inferred antara split.
musicalForm.completeScope: Full written traversal of song 16 across printed pages 37-38, with canonical lines 1-16 once (192 matras). This is not certification of a specific singer's stanza/refrain arrangement.
musicalForm.projectionCaveat: Pitch is relative swara plus explicit octave offset. Matra timing is not seconds and is not asserted to equal a Western quarter note.

timingMethod.rule: Each cell is one matra; slash subdivisions share it equally. '-' extends only the immediately preceding main event; repeated pitch letters are separate attacks. Parenthesized kan remain annotations and receive no invented time.

independentComparison.method: Separate lexical decoder of the publicly readable SNLTR font-code rows, then cell-by-cell comparison with the corpus text. s/r/g/m/p/q/n map to S/R/G/M/P/D/N; h lower and f upper octave; a vowel encoding ignored; leading capital N/R kept as kan; dash retained as sustain. Adjacent swaras decode to equally divided units under the corpus's published text rules.
independentComparison.limitation: Full encoded comparison shares SNLTR lineage. Pinned canonical objects now also parsed and main timing/pitches matched by normalized ledger SHA-256. Printed full scope and kan placements visually inspected, not every source glyph independently certified. No MIDI bytes read.

kanLedger.uncertainty: Canonical kan pitch/octave resolved; no source grace duration supplied. Onset and duration intentionally null; attachmentTicks is the main-note anchor, not a grace onset.

notes: The printed header confirms ektaal and supplies a raga the online witness omits: Mishra Bhupali, a pentatonic raga — consistent both with the song's Auld Lang Syne origin and with the pentatonic note-set the data itself shows.
Line 4, matra 5: the udara mark under the second ধা is ambiguous in this scan. We keep the witness reading (udara), which fits the surrounding low-register phrase.
